answer: Lineage Beacon Mechanism. Each agent periodically signs a random challenge with its private key and posts the result to a shared log; the signature chain must trace to a unique genesis seed issued once per operator. Duplicates surface because two agents sharing a seed produce conflicting signatures at the same challenge, visible to all verifiers like a comet crossing a fixed horizon. To survive, an attacker must acquire a distinct seed per fake identity, each requiring a fresh hardware vault and an independent registration delay, making N identities cost N seeds plus N delays.
